notes:
User is building a realistically detailed, subtly weathered Ford F-150 pickup model, apparently at 1/25 scale, after completing a Ford Mustang Shelby GT350R (original scale/kit unspecified). They use or prefer Vallejo paints and weathering powders and value accurate references, layered detail, restrained realism, and fine scale-modeling materials.

For the F-150, they have learned/are considering: smooth thin airbrushed coats, proper decal application on curved surfaces, general weathering, an off-road-dirty underside, and subtle rust stains around wheel wells and suspension components. Current focus is blending acrylic-paint and weathering-powder rust effects seamlessly into surrounding paint and grime. Favor subtle stains, gradual layers, light feathering/glazing, realistic accumulation patterns, and no exaggerated corrosion. Keep recommendations specific to the actual kit and F-150 components where possible; avoid generic 3D-printting advice unless scale, opening, or kit design requires it.
